salt_concord_brineguard.name: Brineguard
salt_concord_brineguard.description: The salt-crusted spear line that paved the Shelf one road at a time. Alone it is a farmer with a pole; shoulder to shoulder it is a wall.

salt_concord_salt_levy.name: Salt Levy
salt_concord_salt_levy.description: Conscripted by the road-tax and given a spear. Cheap, plentiful, and exactly as brave as the line around them.

salt_concord_surveyor.name: Surveyor
salt_concord_surveyor.description: The Concord owns what it has measured. Surveyors chalk enemies onto the map before the line ever moves.

salt_concord_brine_slinger.name: Brine Slinger
salt_concord_brine_slinger.description: A miner turned skirmisher who flings pans of cut brine. A hit leaves armour weeping and rust-red.

salt_concord_saltwright.name: Saltwright
salt_concord_saltwright.description: Salt-alchemist and mason in one. Saltwrights grow barricades from the dry flats in an afternoon, and cut the enemy's road to the Rim in two.

salt_concord_causeway_outrider.name: Causeway Outrider
salt_concord_causeway_outrider.description: Mounted courier of the salt roads. Outriders run down stragglers that break from their own formations.

salt_concord_brine_chirurgeon.name: Brine Chirurgeon
salt_concord_brine_chirurgeon.description: Field surgeon who cleans wounds with brine and swears by it. The line holds because someone keeps stitching it.

salt_concord_tollkeeper.name: Tollkeeper
salt_concord_tollkeeper.description: Every road has a toll and every toll has a keeper. They reel in those who try to cross without paying.

salt_concord_stair_warden.name: Stair-Warden
salt_concord_stair_warden.description: Sworn to the Greywater Stair, and to the idea that nothing climbs it uninvited. Neighbours stand taller beside them.

salt_concord_caustic_lantern.name: Caustic Lantern
salt_concord_caustic_lantern.description: A wheeled brazier that hurls burning salt-glass in long arcs. Slow, loud, and expensive to defend.

salt_concord_rim_marshal.name: Rim Marshal
salt_concord_rim_marshal.description: Officer of the Rim Wardens, rank earned in road-surveys and border wars. Where the Marshal stands, the formation remembers its drill.

salt_concord_saltmill_juggernaut.name: Saltmill Juggernaut
salt_concord_saltmill_juggernaut.description: A salt-grinding mill bolted to iron treads and sent against the enemy line. The Concord's proof that a road can walk.

salt_concord_tamsin_orrel.name: Commander Tamsin Orrel
salt_concord_tamsin_orrel.title: Surveyor-Commander of Lantern Shoal
salt_concord_tamsin_orrel.description: A Rim Marshal's daughter and the youngest survey-company commander the Concord has, promoted because nobody senior would take the Shoal. She measures everything twice and keeps a night lamp lit, and she wants to hold the work together even if the paper does not.

salt_concord_hesper_vael.name: Warden-General Hesper Vael
salt_concord_hesper_vael.title: Marshal of the Greywater Stair
salt_concord_hesper_vael.description: Oldest living Stair-Warden, who has stood the top landing of the Greywater Stair for forty years and has never once given up a step. She wants one thing, which is that nothing climbs the Stair uninvited, and she will outlast anyone who tries.

salt_concord_ione_karst.name: Magister Ione Karst
salt_concord_ione_karst.title: Assayer of the Saltpan Verge
salt_concord_ione_karst.description: Chief salt-alchemist of the Verge, who has tasted every brine on the Shelf and trusts none of them. She wants a pure salt, one that holds the line without the people who dig it dying of it, and she will test every enemy as a sample.

hadal_court_pit_thrall.name: Pit Thrall
hadal_court_pit_thrall.description: Brine-grown labourer of the vent pools, bred to fill a breach in the line and be walked over by something larger. The Court counts them as the floor its champions stand on.

hadal_court_bell_knight.name: Bell-Knight
hadal_court_bell_knight.description: A knight sealed inside a brass pressure-bell that keeps the trench weight in and the Ebb out. It walks ahead of the Court so the bell's toll is the first thing the enemy hears.

hadal_court_lurecaller.name: Lurecaller
hadal_court_lurecaller.description: Carries a lamp-stalk grown from its own skull and swings it to draw the curious into reach. In the Court's hunts it is the one who decides where the prey will stand.

hadal_court_lantern_spitter.name: Lantern Spitter
hadal_court_lantern_spitter.description: A glass-skinned gulper that spits luminous brine. Fired from behind the bells, it is how the Court teaches the sunlit to fear a sudden flash.

hadal_court_vent_priest.name: Vent-Priest
hadal_court_vent_priest.description: Tends a portable vent-flame that keeps the Court alive far from the trench floor. Its prayers are warm water, and it is the reason the slow giants survive their long climb.

hadal_court_pressure_lancer.name: Pressure Lancer
hadal_court_pressure_lancer.description: Fires bored shafts of compressed brine that carry a little of the deep with them. The Court's artillery, for a people who never forgot what true weight feels like.

hadal_court_murk_diver.name: Murk Diver
hadal_court_murk_diver.description: A lean, quick scout that slips from shadow to shadow ahead of the army. It maps the dark places a Court column will have to cross.

hadal_court_trench_crab.name: Trench Crab
hadal_court_trench_crab.description: A barnacled, house-sized hunter-beast the Court breeds to pin and break the enemy's formation. It guards the roads the great houses use to climb out of the trench.

hadal_court_crushing_maw.name: Crushing Maw
hadal_court_crushing_maw.description: A walking mouth, thousands of years old, that the Court keeps in a tomb of brine and wakes only for war. Nothing that stands before it has ever stood again.

hadal_court_deep_herald.name: Deep Herald
hadal_court_deep_herald.description: Voice of the Court of Depths, who sings the dark across a battlefield before the army arrives. It exists so the enemy forgets the shape of the sky.

hadal_court_tollwarden.name: Tollwarden
hadal_court_tollwarden.description: A magistrate of the Court who carries the weight of its oath into the field. Where the Tollwarden stands, the Court's champions fight as if the whole sea were behind them.

hadal_court_trench_mother.name: Trench Mother
hadal_court_trench_mother.description: The great brood-mother of the trench floors, hauled in a pressure-cradle at the heart of the Court's armies. She is there to prove the Court can raise an army from nothing, and does.

hadal_court_herald_vhaal.name: Herald Vhaal
hadal_court_herald_vhaal.title: The Third Bell of the Court of Depths
hadal_court_herald_vhaal.description: Envoy of the Court of Depths in a bronze brine-bell, formal and slow and unfailingly polite, who treats the surface as a house where a guest has been eating the furniture for three hundred years. She wants one question answered, who lifted the sea, and she will accept only the truth.

hadal_court_orrun_tessk.name: Orrun Tessk
hadal_court_orrun_tessk.title: Knight-Unrelieved of the Seventh Watch
hadal_court_orrun_tessk.description: A Bell-Knight who stood the night watch when the sea vanished and has never been relieved, his bell cracked and still tolling. He wants an officer of the surface to stand in front of him and sign the order that ends his watch.

hadal_court_maelis_quell.name: Maelis Quell
hadal_court_maelis_quell.title: Hearth-Mother of the Warm Vents
hadal_court_maelis_quell.description: Eldest Vent-Priest of the Court, who carried a flame up out of the trench cradled against the cold and has not let it gutter in forty years. She wants to see her giants reach the open sky alive, and to learn whether the surface sea is mercy or theft.

returning_tide_penitent.name: Penitent
returning_tide_penitent.description: A shaven pilgrim who walks into the surf to be forgiven. The Tide spends them freely, and they would have it no other way.

returning_tide_drowned.name: Drowned
returning_tide_drowned.description: One of the faithful dead, kept wet so it can keep walking. It falls once, then gets back up, because the Rim has taught it patience.

returning_tide_tear_slinger.name: Tear-Slinger
returning_tide_tear_slinger.description: A mourner who hurls brine from a bag of collected grief. Its job is to leave enemy lines soaked before the first blade lands.

returning_tide_tideskulker.name: Tideskulker
returning_tide_tideskulker.description: A gutter-child who learned the shallows on the Weeping Shelf. It slips behind lines to cut the legs from anything that moves slowly.

returning_tide_wringer.name: Wringer
returning_tide_wringer.description: A priest of the oldest rite, who draws water from living things and carries it to the sea above. It exists to outlast whatever it holds.

returning_tide_rainsayer.name: Rainsayer
returning_tide_rainsayer.description: A prophet who calls rain from clear sky and floods the ground beneath enemy feet. It claims ground for the faithful and makes it theirs alone.

returning_tide_shroud_mender.name: Shroud-Mender
returning_tide_shroud_mender.description: A midwife of the Drowned who wraps wounds in wet cloth that never dries. It keeps the swarm on its feet long enough to finish its prayers.

returning_tide_anchor_bearer.name: Anchor-Bearer
returning_tide_anchor_bearer.description: A penitent who chose to drag a ship's anchor until the tide took them. It holds the line and drags runners down to the Drowned.

returning_tide_choirmaster.name: Choirmaster
returning_tide_choirmaster.description: A conductor of the faithful whose hymns keep a thousand throats in time. It exists so that cheap bodies fight like one great body.

returning_tide_undertow_singer.name: Undertow Singer
returning_tide_undertow_singer.description: A voice that tugs at ankles. It herds enemies into brine pools and holds them there until the choir arrives.

returning_tide_bloat_drowned.name: Bloat-Drowned
returning_tide_bloat_drowned.description: A corpse left to swell for a season until it carries a river inside. It walks into the enemy line and releases it.

returning_tide_tide_prophet.name: Tide-Prophet
returning_tide_tide_prophet.description: The one who heard the sea above and told the faithful where it went. It drops a flood on the world and does not pretend to be sorry.

returning_tide_imre_dunnock.name: Prophet Imre Dunnock
returning_tide_imre_dunnock.title: the Wet Saint
returning_tide_imre_dunnock.description: Once a Concord tax clerk, he audited the water ledgers, found they did not balance, and walked into the rain with a following of thousands. He wants every lighthouse put out because he believes the sea above will be merciful, and he knows in his gentler hours that it will not.

returning_tide_maren_ketch.name: Sister Maren Ketch
returning_tide_maren_ketch.title: Matron of the Dry Hands
returning_tide_maren_ketch.description: The senior wringer of the Weeping Shelf, who has drawn the water out of more living things than she will admit to counting. She wants the faithful to be worth the sea when it arrives, and keeps what she takes.

returning_tide_oswin_brack.name: Captain Oswin Brack
returning_tide_oswin_brack.title: the Unsunk
returning_tide_oswin_brack.description: A Hulk captain who went down with his ship on the night of the Long Ebb and has refused to stay down for three hundred years. He wants his crew back, all of them, and the Tide has promised him the sea will bring them.

salvage_compact_lamplighter.name: Lamplighter
salvage_compact_lamplighter.description: A hulk-kid with a lantern pole who runs ahead to light the way, and to pour oil where the enemy will step. Cheap, quick, and expected to be lost.

salvage_compact_scrapper.name: Hull Scrapper
salvage_compact_scrapper.description: A deckhand paid in rope and rumour to hold a corridor of rusted plating for exactly as long as the Compact needs.

salvage_compact_wrecker.name: Wrecker
salvage_compact_wrecker.description: Strips wrecks down to the nails and strips enemy lines the same way, in and out before anyone has finished shouting.

salvage_compact_rivet_slinger.name: Rivet-Slinger
salvage_compact_rivet_slinger.description: Fires bent rivets and nails from a pneumatic gun built out of a ship's bilge pump. The Compact pays its marksmen in scrap.

salvage_compact_powder_monk.name: Powder-Monk
salvage_compact_powder_monk.description: Keeper of the leviathan-fat kilns who blesses every fuse before it is lit. Sells fire to everyone, and burns those who do not pay.

salvage_compact_bone_sled_rider.name: Bone-Sled Rider
salvage_compact_bone_sled_rider.description: Rides a sled of leviathan ribs over the salt faster than anyone can aim, carrying messages, cargo, and sudden violence.

salvage_compact_tallow_mender.name: Tallow-Mender
salvage_compact_tallow_mender.description: Hull-doctor who patches wounds with rendered fat and greases the boots of those who must run. The Compact's closest thing to a field hospital.

salvage_compact_snare_tinker.name: Snare-Tinker
salvage_compact_snare_tinker.description: Builds every trap the Compact lays for invaders, and every one looks like something worth picking up.

salvage_compact_hullbreaker.name: Hullbreaker
salvage_compact_hullbreaker.description: Sledgehammer-wielder hired to bring down bulkheads, and sometimes the soldiers behind them. The one Compact piece that can hold ground.

salvage_compact_quartermaster.name: Quartermaster
salvage_compact_quartermaster.description: Keeper of the ledger and the cutlass, who pays out shares mid-battle and gets everyone moving at once.

salvage_compact_breach_gunner.name: Breach-Gunner
salvage_compact_breach_gunner.description: Lobs powder kegs from a hull-mounted mortar and shoots anything that survives. Every shot costs more than the average sailor earns in a season.

salvage_compact_harpoon_engine.name: Harpoon Engine
salvage_compact_harpoon_engine.description: A whaling harpoon the size of a mast, bolted to a hull and wound with chain, built to haul anything that moves back to the Compact. It took a generation to build and no one is allowed to sell it.

salvage_compact_odo_brask.name: Odo Brask
salvage_compact_odo_brask.title: Fixer of the Kettle Market
salvage_compact_odo_brask.description: A fat, cheerful broker in three coats who sells maps, grain, rumours and, when it pays, silence. He wants to stay solvent and alive, and has found that the two usually mean selling someone out at the right price.

salvage_compact_ketta_vane.name: Ketta Vane
salvage_compact_ketta_vane.title: Sled-Queen of the Long Salt
salvage_compact_ketta_vane.description: The fastest rider on the salt, who has outrun three debts, two wars and her own reputation on a sled of leviathan ribs. She wants a stretch of open flat with nobody on it, and will burn anything that stands between her and it.

salvage_compact_brother_ashmaw.name: Brother Ashmaw
salvage_compact_brother_ashmaw.title: Fat-Cook of the Burning Chapel
salvage_compact_brother_ashmaw.description: Head of the Powder-Monks, who renders leviathan fat into the finest blasting grease in the Hulks and blesses every barrel by name. He wants the old hulls to burn bright enough to be seen from the Rim, so that someone finally asks what the Compact has been guarding.

reef_ascendant_polyp_drone.name: Polyp Drone
reef_ascendant_polyp_drone.description: One mouth of the colony, grown in an hour and spent in a minute. The Reef does not mourn drones; it grows more.

reef_ascendant_spitter_polyp.name: Spitter Polyp
reef_ascendant_spitter_polyp.description: A drone bred to lob caustic calcite slurry from behind the line. It exists so the front drones can die with company.

reef_ascendant_fanblade.name: Fanblade
reef_ascendant_fanblade.description: A drone grown around a fan of razored calcite. It is the colony's reach, sent to cut down whatever the slow bodies cannot catch.

reef_ascendant_sting_anemone.name: Sting Anemone
reef_ascendant_sting_anemone.description: A rooted-looking thing that is not rooted at all. Its touch dulls the nerves of anything that threatens a mind.

reef_ascendant_shard_urchin.name: Shard Urchin
reef_ascendant_shard_urchin.description: A drone that bristles when cornered. The colony plants it in doorways so that passing through costs blood.

reef_ascendant_brainstalk.name: Brainstalk
reef_ascendant_brainstalk.description: A fluted tower of living calcite that thinks for the drones around it. Kill it and every body within its reach goes slack.

reef_ascendant_broodspire.name: Broodspire
reef_ascendant_broodspire.description: A budding spire that pushes out fresh drones the way a reef pushes out polyps. It is the reason the Reef is never really outnumbered.

reef_ascendant_reef_tender.name: Reef Tender
reef_ascendant_reef_tender.description: A drone bred to feed its siblings from the colony's stores. It is the only mercy the Reef knows, and it is still just bookkeeping.

reef_ascendant_spireguard.name: Spireguard
reef_ascendant_spireguard.description: A drone that never stops growing, layer on layer of calcite, until it is more wall than animal. The colony plants it in the road and waits.

reef_ascendant_calcite_bloom.name: Calcite Bloom
reef_ascendant_calcite_bloom.description: A flower the size of a house, its roots turning bare rock into Living Reef. Where it blooms the Reef is already home.

reef_ascendant_lensbearer.name: Lensbearer
reef_ascendant_lensbearer.description: A colony grown around a lens of clear calcite that gathers the sun the Reef woke to. It sees far and burns what it sees.

reef_ascendant_elder_colony.name: Elder Colony
reef_ascendant_elder_colony.description: One of the oldest minds on the Shelf, thinking a single slow thought for three centuries. Wherever it stands, the Reef is one body.

reef_ascendant_coralspire.name: Coralspire
reef_ascendant_coralspire.title: The Mind of Coralspire
reef_ascendant_coralspire.description: Coralspire is the eldest colony of the Shelf, a petrified reef that woke at the first dawn and has thought slowly ever since. It wants the Ebb to last forever, because it can feel its own oldest branches crumbling as the sea stays gone.

reef_ascendant_marrowbloom.name: Marrowbloom
reef_ascendant_marrowbloom.title: The Slow Hunger of the Shelf
reef_ascendant_marrowbloom.description: Marrowbloom is a colony woken in a mass grave of wrecks, and it has learned that everything dead leaves calcite behind. It wants to eat the whole battlefield down to bare reef before the sea can come back for it.

reef_ascendant_glasswake.name: Glasswake
reef_ascendant_glasswake.title: The Lensmind of the Glass Shallows
reef_ascendant_glasswake.description: Glasswake is a young colony grown in clear stone lenses that bend the first sunlight into sight, and it remembers every shape that ever crossed its focus. It wants to see the end of every lighthouse, because the beams make its lenses ache.

lanternkeepers_wick.name: Wick
lanternkeepers_wick.description: The youngest keeper on every stair, sent ahead with a taper to see what the beam will meet. A Wick's whole job is to be the first light on a thing.

lanternkeepers_lamplit_sailor.name: Lamplit Sailor
lanternkeepers_lamplit_sailor.description: A drowned sailor the beam revealed and the lamp bound, who serves because the lamp is all that stands between it and the sea. Keepers summon them by the dozen and do not learn their names.

lanternkeepers_oilbearer.name: Oilbearer
lanternkeepers_oilbearer.description: The keeper who carries the lamp-oil up three hundred steps and the cudgel to guard it. A spill on the stairs is also a weapon.

lanternkeepers_signalman.name: Signalman
lanternkeepers_signalman.description: Flashes shutter-codes between lighthouses across the dark water. In battle the flash lands on an enemy and every other keeper knows exactly where to aim.

lanternkeepers_beaconrunner.name: Beaconrunner
lanternkeepers_beaconrunner.description: Carries word between lamps faster than any boat, by stepping along the beams themselves. Where a beam is, a Beaconrunner can be.

lanternkeepers_lantern_warden.name: Lantern Warden
lanternkeepers_lantern_warden.description: Tends the flame that tends the keepers: every wound is closed in lamplight and every vigil is shared. Wardens go where the lamp is dimmest.

lanternkeepers_stairkeeper.name: Stairkeeper
lanternkeepers_stairkeeper.description: Sworn to a single staircase and to the door at its top. Three centuries of climbing have left nothing in the Stairkeeper that can be pushed down it.

lanternkeepers_glassgrinder.name: Glassgrinder
lanternkeepers_glassgrinder.description: Cuts and polishes the great lenses, and knows precisely how to turn one into a blinding flash. Enemies that stare into a Glassgrinder's work do not stare long.

lanternkeepers_bellringer.name: Bellringer
lanternkeepers_bellringer.description: Rings the fog-bell that wakes the Lamplit from the water. Each toll calls another drowned sailor to the lamp's side.

lanternkeepers_beamwright.name: Beamwright
lanternkeepers_beamwright.description: Builds and aims the great beams, trimming the lens until a line of light is as sharp as a drawn blade. Everything in its path is revealed, and most of it does not survive that.

lanternkeepers_keeper_of_the_long_watch.name: Keeper of the Long Watch
lanternkeepers_keeper_of_the_long_watch.description: Head of a lighthouse garrison, who has not slept a full night in forty years and does not intend to start. The Long Watch is the vow, and the Keeper is the vow made flesh.

lanternkeepers_first_flame.name: First Flame
lanternkeepers_first_flame.description: The flame that was already lit on the night of the Long Ebb, burning in a lamp nobody had touched. It is the oldest Keeper there is, and it has never been quiet.

lanternkeepers_keeper_pell_auster.name: Keeper Pell Auster
lanternkeepers_keeper_pell_auster.title: Last Keeper of Lantern Shoal
lanternkeepers_keeper_pell_auster.description: Elderly, half-blind and never asleep, Pell is the last Lanternkeeper of the Shoal and the one who knows exactly what the lamp holds up. She wants every lamp lit and every stranger kept from it, and she will stand in front of any blade to see it done.

lanternkeepers_lensmaster_oriel_venn.name: Lensmaster Oriel Venn
lanternkeepers_lensmaster_oriel_venn.title: Mistress of the Seventh Lens
lanternkeepers_lensmaster_oriel_venn.description: Venn grinds and aims the great lamp lenses, and can fold a beacon's beam into a blade of light a mile long. She wants to prove that a keeper can strike as well as watch, before the vow of silence cuts her order's last hope down.

lanternkeepers_captain_hollis_drenn.name: Captain Hollis Drenn
lanternkeepers_captain_hollis_drenn.title: First of the Drowned Watch
lanternkeepers_captain_hollis_drenn.description: Hollis went down with the last ship to founder off the Rim and woke bound to a lighthouse lamp, now commanding the Lamplit who share his fate. He wants to keep the beam burning so that the sea above never gets to finish what it started.

keystone.name: Beacon
keystone.description: A stranded lighthouse, still lit. It holds the sea off this stretch of the Ebb.

overcurrent_bellyeye_shoal.name: Bellyeye Shoal
overcurrent_bellyeye_shoal.description: A knot of hand-sized pale fish with a wet pink eye on every belly, turning as one animal toward anything that glows. They fall by the hundred and eat what they land on.

overcurrent_gulper.name: Gulper
overcurrent_gulper.description: An eel that is mostly mouth, the jaw unhinging to three times the length of its body. It does not chew; it closes around a thing and waits for the thing to stop.

overcurrent_tongue_louse.name: Tongue-Louse
overcurrent_tongue_louse.description: A dog-sized parasitic isopod, glassy and many-legged, that crawls into a mouth and replaces the tongue. It lives on the blood of whatever it is bolted to.

overcurrent_driftbell.name: Driftbell
overcurrent_driftbell.description: A translucent jelly the size of a cart, its organs plainly visible and pulsing, trailing threads that hang the length of a street. It drifts over a battlefield like a slow cold bruise.

overcurrent_lure_mother.name: Lure-Mother
overcurrent_lure_mother.description: An anglerfish whose lure has learned to look exactly like a lighthouse beam. Things walk toward it weeping with relief, and the mouth behind it is very patient.

overcurrent_hagwyrm.name: Hagwyrm
overcurrent_hagwyrm.description: A hagfish the length of a wagon, knotted like a rope and slick with a slime that sets around anything that touches it. It does not fight so much as fill the space where you were.

overcurrent_siphon_chain.name: Siphon Chain
overcurrent_siphon_chain.description: A siphonophore strung across the air, a hundred lantern-bodies sharing one nerve, each stinging bell lit from inside. It is not one animal and has never been alone.

overcurrent_weeping_sunfish.name: Weeping Sunfish
overcurrent_weeping_sunfish.description: A vast, slow, flat moon of a fish, its flank bruised with parasites, weeping brine from both eyes without end. The others crowd under it to be rained on.

overcurrent_downward_shark.name: Downward Shark
overcurrent_downward_shark.description: A frilled, goblin-jawed shark that falls point-first, rows of needle teeth already open, jaws cocked forward on a ligament. It reaches the ground before its scream does.

overcurrent_barrelgaze.name: Barrelgaze
overcurrent_barrelgaze.description: A fish with a clear dome for a head, the brain visible inside, and two green eyes that roll upward through its own skull to track the beam. Where it stares, the shoal strikes.

overcurrent_ribbon_king.name: Ribbon King
overcurrent_ribbon_king.description: An oarfish thirty feet long, silver and boneless, crowned in a crest of red filaments that streams behind it like blood in water. It slides through a battle line without once seeming to move.

overcurrent_the_thinning.name: The Thinning
overcurrent_the_thinning.description: A ray so vast its shadow lands a turn before it does, its pale belly alive with a field of watching eyes and its mouth a slot the width of a wall. Where it passes, the floor of the sky is thin.

overcurrent_mother_mantle.name: Mother Mantle
overcurrent_mother_mantle.title: the Hook-Armed Deep
overcurrent_mother_mantle.description: A colossal squid whose suckers turn out to be rotating hooks, with an eye the size of a door that never blinks and a beak that works behind the arms. She fell through the thinning sky holding two ships' worth of drowned crew, and she has not let go.

overcurrent_saint_rictus.name: Saint Rictus
overcurrent_saint_rictus.title: the Jaw That Prays
overcurrent_saint_rictus.description: A goblin shark whose jaw slings out on a ligament longer than its body, fed by a Tide splinter that kneels on the shore and calls it a saint. It has understood exactly one thing about worship, which is that it is dinner.

overcurrent_the_undersinging.name: The Undersinging
overcurrent_the_undersinging.title: what feeds below the beam
overcurrent_the_undersinging.description: A siphonophore choir a hundred bodies long, every bell humming the exact pitch of the lamps, strung down the dark like a drowned cathedral organ. The Lanternkeepers' Vigil Book keeps a locked page about it.

gyre_roost_runner.name: Roost-Runner
gyre_roost_runner.description: A roost kid on a half-tame gull, sent to lift a purse, a map or a boot off anything that stops moving. The Gyre sends them in first because nobody has ever caught one.

gyre_salt_crow.name: Salt Crow
gyre_salt_crow.description: A crow the size of a hunting dog that has learned exactly how long a wounded thing takes to stop kicking. Roost-folk keep them for company, and for cleaning up.

gyre_gullwife.name: Gullwife
gyre_gullwife.description: A cliff-woman who keeps a flock of screaming gulls in her apron and throws it at whatever she dislikes. She has been in forty fights and has never once been hit by her own birds.

gyre_roostwarden.name: Roostwarden
gyre_roostwarden.description: A cliff-guard in feathered oilskin with a hooked nest-pike, who holds the ground the birds cannot. When the wheel is overhead, he is the one who stays put.

gyre_skua_lancer.name: Skua Lancer
gyre_skua_lancer.description: A rider on a hook-beaked skua, trained to drop on anything already bleeding and be gone before it turns around. They pick their targets the way a creditor does.

gyre_pelican_hauler.name: Pelican Hauler
gyre_pelican_hauler.description: An enormous pelican whose pouch holds a fisherman, a goat or a Concord marksman, in that order of complaint. Roost-folk use it to fetch the enemy and to ferry their own across the gaps.

gyre_windreader.name: Windreader
gyre_windreader.description: An old roost-reader with a kite-staff, who reads the wrong-coloured sky the way other people read faces. She tells the wheel when to dive and the wounded when to keep still.

gyre_shrike_harrier.name: Shrike Harrier
gyre_shrike_harrier.description: A rider on a shrike that keeps its larder on salt-spikes, and has been taught to treat a battlefield as a larder too. What it spikes stays where it was put.

gyre_wheel_captain.name: Wheel-Captain
gyre_wheel_captain.description: The leader of a wheel of riders, on a black-backed gull the colour of a funeral coat. She does not give orders; she circles, and the others learn what that means.

gyre_frigate_thief.name: Frigate Thief
gyre_frigate_thief.description: A rider on a red-throated frigatebird, the thief of the air, who steals from the Tide itself. Every faction on the Rim has a Frigate Thief story and every one of them ends with an empty purse.

gyre_stormkite_gunner.name: Stormkite Gunner
gyre_stormkite_gunner.description: A gunner on a kite-platform tethered to the cliff, firing harpoon-bolts down from a height. The platform will not leave the ground, and neither will the gunner's opinion of anyone who calls it a toy.

gyre_mother_of_the_wheel.name: Mother of the Wheel
gyre_mother_of_the_wheel.description: An albatross the size of a sail-barge and the eldest bird on the Rim, said to have taught the first gull to follow a ship. When her shadow crosses the field every rider in the Gyre knows which way to turn.

gyre_wren_halloway.name: Wren Halloway
gyre_wren_halloway.title: the Rimfall Thief
gyre_wren_halloway.description: A young roost-thief on a frigatebird who has robbed the Concord, the Compact and, once, famously, a Lanternkeeper. She wants a score so big the whole Rim has to admit she was the one who took it.

gyre_roost_mother_oskeline.name: Roost-Mother Oskeline
gyre_roost_mother_oskeline.title: Keeper of the High Nests
gyre_roost_mother_oskeline.description: An ancient woman who has raised every great bird on her cliff and can call any of them by the sound of her knees. She wants her nests safe and her chicks fed, and she is prepared to be unpleasant about it.

gyre_captain_torr_ashby.name: Captain Torr Ashby
gyre_captain_torr_ashby.title: of the Black Wheel
gyre_captain_torr_ashby.description: A mercenary who rides a vast bald vulture and follows armies for the dead, selling the Rim's battles their own cleanup. He wants only what every scavenger wants: for the fighting to last a little longer.

gyre_cormorant_diver.name: Cormorant Diver
gyre_cormorant_diver.description: Dives under the salt crust like it was water and comes up where nobody was looking. The Gyre says a cormorant is a gull that has seen the bottom.

gyre_guano_bombardier.name: Guano Bombardier
gyre_guano_bombardier.description: Drops jars from on high and does not wait to see them land. The jars are guano, mostly. The rest is a Gyre secret and smells worse.

gyre_kite_rigger.name: Kite-Rigger
gyre_kite_rigger.description: Strings kites and perches along the high ground until the Gyre has a sky to stand on. She hums while she works, a song about someone who never came back down.

gyre_linnet_garr.name: Linnet Garr
gyre_linnet_garr.title: the Rider Who Delivers
gyre_linnet_garr.description: The messenger from the Lanternkeeper campaign, the rider who never breaks the Gyre's oldest bargain: what is carried is delivered. She will carry you out of a fight too, if you ask nicely.

hadal_court_bell_bearer.name: Bell-Bearer
hadal_court_bell_bearer.description: Two thralls haul a pressure-bell on chains, and the Court's giants ride in its shadow. Anything the Bell swings over is simply moved, and nobody argues with the Bell.

hadal_court_anglet.name: Anglet
hadal_court_anglet.description: A small lantern-jawed pressure-born that spits glowing bile at anything that looks warm. It would be frightening if it were bigger. It is aware of this.

hadal_court_silt_weaver.name: Silt-Weaver
hadal_court_silt_weaver.description: Trails trench silt from long gill-veils and lays it down in drifts the colour of a held breath. The floor is a thing the Court has always owned, and the Silt-Weaver is how it collects.

hadal_court_justiciar_oulme.name: Oulme
hadal_court_justiciar_oulme.title: Justiciar, the Second Bell
hadal_court_justiciar_oulme.description: The Court's judge, who carries the indictment of the surface in a pressure-casket and has not yet found it empty. She does not hate the sunlit world. She has read the charges.

lanternkeepers_foghorn_crew.name: Foghorn Crew
lanternkeepers_foghorn_crew.description: Two keepers on a hand-cranked horn, one at the crank and one watching the fog. When the reefs come up out of the dark, they are the first to say so, loudly.

lanternkeepers_wreck_light.name: Wreck-Light
lanternkeepers_wreck_light.description: The keepers' oldest secret: a lamp hung where no lamp should be, to put a ship on the rocks. They do not talk about it, and they have not stopped.

lanternkeepers_lens_apprentice.name: Lens-Apprentice
lanternkeepers_lens_apprentice.description: Glass-dust on her apron, a cracked lens in her hand, and a lamp she has not yet learned to keep from flickering. The Bellringer calls her a promising girl.

lanternkeepers_sabeth_moor.name: Archivist Sabeth Moor
lanternkeepers_sabeth_moor.title: Keeper of the Archive
lanternkeepers_sabeth_moor.description: Keeper of the Archive, and the only one living who has read the true logbooks of the Long Ebb. She speaks quietly now, as someone does who knows what is written in them.

overcurrent_rainmoth_cloud.name: Rainmoth Cloud
overcurrent_rainmoth_cloud.description: A shoal of grey moths that carries its own weather. They shed rain on whoever stands beneath, friend or not, and it has never once been a mistake.

overcurrent_cloudwhale_calf.name: Cloudwhale Calf
overcurrent_cloudwhale_calf.description: A young cloud-whale, slow and enormous, still learning that the sky is not meant to be walked on. What it lands on is flattened and what it stands beside is moved.

overcurrent_stormglass_squid.name: Stormglass Squid
overcurrent_stormglass_squid.description: A squid with lightning in its glass-clear mantle, fallen from the high cold where the storms are born. It does not aim so much as release.

overcurrent_old_sounding.name: Old Sounding
overcurrent_old_sounding.title: the Whale That Climbed Back
overcurrent_old_sounding.description: An ancient cloud-whale that fell once already and climbed back, and has no intention of leaving the sea again. Where it stands, the old rain stays.

reef_ascendant_mantis_striker.name: Mantis Striker
reef_ascendant_mantis_striker.description: A mantis shrimp grown in living calcite, its club a knuckle of the same stuff the Reef builds walls from. It hits once, and what it hits stops being a wall.

reef_ascendant_spore_drifter.name: Spore Drifter
reef_ascendant_spore_drifter.description: A coral jelly that drifts on warm updrafts and drops where the colony wants a footing. The Reef sends it first and grows where it lands.

reef_ascendant_siphon_sponge.name: Siphon Sponge
reef_ascendant_siphon_sponge.description: A pulsing sponge-mound that drinks whatever walks past. What it filters out of the enemy it passes to the nearest drone, because the Reef wastes nothing.

reef_ascendant_the_bleached.name: The Bleached
reef_ascendant_the_bleached.title: The White Mind
reef_ascendant_the_bleached.description: A mind-coral that turned white in the sun and is starving. It still thinks for the drones around it, and it has begun to think of them as food.

returning_tide_ferryman.name: Ferryman
returning_tide_ferryman.description: Rows a dry boat across the salt on runners, humming the fare. Whoever he carries over comes back a little wetter, and somehow never complains of the crossing.

returning_tide_cistern_wife.name: Cistern-Wife
returning_tide_cistern_wife.description: Carries a cracked cistern on her back that never empties and never says whose water it was. Where she stops to rest the ground remembers the sea.

returning_tide_salt_drinker.name: Salt-Drinker
returning_tide_salt_drinker.description: A penitent who swallowed brine until it killed them, and kept walking. They are very full. They are going to be somebody else's problem soon.

returning_tide_ash_harrowgate.name: Ash Harrowgate
returning_tide_ash_harrowgate.title: Deacon of the Returning Tide
returning_tide_ash_harrowgate.description: Dunnock's enforcer, who wrings the doubters first and gently. He does not shout. The congregation stands closer when he speaks, which is how he knows it is working.

salt_concord_rainwatch_inquisitor.name: Rainwatch Inquisitor
salt_concord_rainwatch_inquisitor.description: The Concord's answer to the Tide's rain-shrines, in white oilcloth with a salt censer on a chain. Where the Inquisitor walks, a sermon goes dry in the middle of a word.

salt_concord_salt_sapper.name: Salt Sapper
salt_concord_salt_sapper.description: Mine-crew with a barrow of salt charges and a short fuse. The Concord builds roads and walls; the Sappers are the ones who are asked to take them down again.

salt_concord_verge_lancer.name: Verge Lancer
salt_concord_verge_lancer.description: Heavy horse of the Verge forts in salt-scaled barding. A Lancer wants a straight road and a clear target, and takes a long moment to forgive either being missing.

salt_concord_abel_pryce.name: Abel Pryce
salt_concord_abel_pryce.title: Surveyor-Royal of the Salt Concord
salt_concord_abel_pryce.description: The Concord's chief cartographer, who measured every waterline mark on the Shelf and quietly knows the Ebb is not permanent. He keeps the survey exact and his conclusions to himself.

salvage_compact_ballast_diver.name: Ballast Diver
salvage_compact_ballast_diver.description: Wreck-diver in a riveted copper suit with lead boots, who walks the sea floor like a man late for a funeral. It takes a lot to move him, and he has a crowbar for whatever else needs shifting.

salvage_compact_kettle_broker.name: Kettle Broker
salvage_compact_kettle_broker.description: Sells to everyone and cheats everyone, and has a kettle on in case it is ever called a conversation. Weak in a fight, which is why the rest of the crew is so careful to keep him alive.

salvage_compact_fat_renderer.name: Fat-Renderer
salvage_compact_fat_renderer.description: Boils leviathan fat into powder in a vat chained to a cart. The smell arrives about a minute before the Renderer does, and about a minute before the fire.

salvage_compact_hesk_varrow.name: Hesk Varrow
salvage_compact_hesk_varrow.title: The Forger
salvage_compact_hesk_varrow.role: The Forger of the Salvage Compact
salvage_compact_hesk_varrow.description: The broker from the paper swords, before the Concord caught him, with a quill behind one ear and a knife behind the other. Every order he has signed is real, in the sense that someone obeyed it.

hermitage_bare_small.name: Bare Scuttler
hermitage_bare_small.description: A dog-sized hermit crab with its soft curled tail out in the air for everyone to see. It is embarrassed, it is furious, and it is very quick.

hermitage_bare_medium.name: Bare Snapper
hermitage_bare_medium.description: A pony-sized crab caught without a house, tail curled tight, one great violet claw held up like a grievance. It wants a shell, and failing that, yours.

hermitage_bare_large.name: Bare Brute
hermitage_bare_large.description: A crab the size of a dray-horse turned out of its gun or its wheelhouse, pale tail dragging, claws wide. Nobody on the Ebb has ever wanted to be the reason.

hermitage_bare_great.name: Bare Giant
hermitage_bare_great.description: A crab as big as a hay-wagon with nothing on its back for the first time in a century. It is looking for the one who did this, and then for somewhere to live.

hermitage_duchess_bare.name: Duchess Abaft, Bare
hermitage_duchess_bare.title: the Stern Tenant
hermitage_duchess_bare.description: The Duchess out of her stern-castle, enormous and pale and absolutely not receiving visitors. Her quarterdeck manner survives the loss of the quarterdeck.

hermitage_knell_bare.name: Old Knell, Bare
hermitage_knell_bare.title: the Grudge-Bell
hermitage_knell_bare.description: Old Knell without its bell, which it will tell you about. At length. After it has dealt with you.

hermitage_sixpence_bare.name: Sixpence, Bare
hermitage_sixpence_bare.title: the Queue-Jumper
hermitage_sixpence_bare.description: Sixpence between kegs, which is how Sixpence likes it best: light, quick, and first to whatever is going.

hermitage_empty_barrel.name: Empty Barrel
hermitage_empty_barrel.description: A tarred hogshead with the bung knocked out and the inside worn smooth. Vacant; apply within.

hermitage_empty_diving_bell.name: Empty Diving Bell
hermitage_empty_diving_bell.description: A brass diving bell standing open-mouthed on the salt, portholes dark. It still smells of the last tenant.

hermitage_empty_bell.name: Empty Bell
hermitage_empty_bell.description: A cracked bronze chapel bell lying on its lip, clapper tied up with rope so it does not ring for nobody.

hermitage_empty_boiler.name: Empty Boiler
hermitage_empty_boiler.description: A riveted ship's boiler on its side with the firebox door hanging open, still warm. Good for a crab who likes it hot.

hermitage_empty_cannon.name: Empty Cannon
hermitage_empty_cannon.description: A Concord long gun with its carriage gone, lying on the salt with the breech open. The best address in the queue.

hermitage_hopeful.name: Hopeful
hermitage_hopeful.description: A young crab with no house at all, sent to the front of the fight because the front is where the wrecks are. Every Hopeful is in the queue for something.

hermitage_barrel_squatter.name: Barrel Squatter
hermitage_barrel_squatter.description: A dog-sized crab in a tarred brewer's hogshead, the first rung of the Hermitage's ladder. Every crab on the Ebb has lived in a barrel once and none of them talk about it.

hermitage_jug_lobber.name: Jug Lobber
hermitage_jug_lobber.description: A crab in a stoneware cistern-jug that throws ballast stones with its big claw. The Compact pay it in jugs, which it considers the deal of the century.

hermitage_lobster_pot_lurker.name: Lobster-Pot Lurker
hermitage_lobster_pot_lurker.description: A crab that moved into a giant iron-and-withy lobster pot and kept the rope. It finds the irony delicious, and so, eventually, does whatever it hauls in.

hermitage_diving_bell_hermit.name: Diving-Bell Hermit
hermitage_diving_bell_hermit.description: A pony-sized crab in a brass salvage diving bell, eyestalks up the inside of the portholes. It holds a line the way a doorstop holds a door.

hermitage_bell_tenant.name: Bell Tenant
hermitage_bell_tenant.description: A crab that took a chapel bell off the Greywater Stair and has rung it, loudly, at everyone since. The Concord still sends letters.

hermitage_boiler_lodger.name: Boiler Lodger
hermitage_boiler_lodger.description: A crab living in a steamer's boiler with a banked fire still going in the box, kept fed on wreck-timber. It likes the warmth and it likes to share.

hermitage_tool_chest_tinker.name: Tool-Chest Tinker
hermitage_tool_chest_tinker.description: A crab in a ship's carpenter's chest with the lid propped open on a chisel, mallet in its claw. It mends shells for the queue and takes payment in nails.

hermitage_lifeboat_skimmer.name: Lifeboat Skimmer
hermitage_lifeboat_skimmer.description: A crab under an upturned clinker lifeboat, legs out beneath it like oars, skidding across the salt on the keel. Every wreck on the Hulks had one of these, and now most of them have a tenant.

hermitage_strongbox_bailiff.name: Strongbox Bailiff
hermitage_strongbox_bailiff.description: A crab in an iron-banded Compact pay-chest, lid raised like a visor, padlock swinging on its chain. It keeps the Hermitage's list of grudges and it serves every one of them in person.

hermitage_gun_deck_lodger.name: Gun-Deck Lodger
hermitage_gun_deck_lodger.description: A horse-sized crab living in a Concord long gun, claws out of the breech, eyestalks either side of the muzzle. It worked out the powder on its own and nobody is happy about that.

hermitage_prow_ram.name: Prow Ram
hermitage_prow_ram.description: A crab wearing the whole bow of a ship, iron ram low, a carved figurehead staring out ahead of it. It has never once gone round anything.

hermitage_wheelhouse_warden.name: Wheelhouse Warden
hermitage_wheelhouse_warden.description: A crab in a coaster's wheelhouse, the great wheel turning in its window as it walks. It keeps the queue, settles who gets which shell, and is obeyed because nobody wants the job.

hermitage_shell_broker.name: Shell-Broker
hermitage_shell_broker.description: A bare crab who never keeps a house, dragging a net-sledge of barrels and spare plate. It sets the price of every shell on the Ebb, and the price is always 'one size up'.

hermitage_the_landlord.name: The Landlord
hermitage_the_landlord.description: A crab as big as a wagon wearing the lamp-room of a fallen lighthouse, the lamp still lit inside it and turning. The Lanternkeepers want it back more than they will say.

hermitage_duchess_abaft.name: Duchess Abaft
hermitage_duchess_abaft.title: the Stern Tenant
hermitage_duchess_abaft.description: The eldest crab on the Hulks, living in the carved stern-castle of a sunk ship-of-the-line, gallery windows lit, rudder for a tail. She owns the Hermitage's longest grudge and its best view.

hermitage_mother_harrow.name: Mother Harrow
hermitage_mother_harrow.title: the Hermit of the Kettle
hermitage_mother_harrow.description: A retired Compact ship's carpenter who walked out into the Kettle forty years ago to mend crabs' shells and never came back. The Compact called her shack 'the Hermitage', and the name stuck to everything that queued outside it.

hermitage_sixpence.name: Sixpence
hermitage_sixpence.title: the Queue-Jumper
hermitage_sixpence.description: A pony-sized crab in a Compact powder keg, still half full, who has never waited in a line in its life. Every crab in the Hermitage has a grudge against Sixpence, and every one of them wants to be it.

hermitage_old_knell.name: Old Knell
hermitage_old_knell.title: the Grudge-Bell
hermitage_old_knell.description: A huge crab in a pressure-bell carried off from the bell-shrine of Trench Deeplight, which the Hadal Court would like back. Old Knell remembers every wrong ever done to it and tolls once for each.

slough_brinkling.name: Brinkling
slough_brinkling.description: A young Slough a few sheddings old, reared to the height of a man on a coil it has not grown into, with a reed gaff and a buckler cut from its own first skin. The marsh sends its young to the front because the young still heal.

slough_banded_lancer.name: Banded Lancer
slough_banded_lancer.description: A black-and-bone banded krait with a long fang-tipped lance, coiled low behind it like a drawn bow. Lancers walk the edges of the hanging-skin cities and strike anything that steps where the skins are.

slough_spitting_olive.name: Spitting Olive
slough_spitting_olive.description: An olive-green sea snake with a throat sac of venom and no patience, who spits for the eyes from four tiles off and is gone before you can see again. The Slough keep them on the reed-towers as other people keep dogs.

slough_reedrunner.name: Reedrunner
slough_reedrunner.description: A thin, fast yellow-lipped krait who carries messages between the hanging cities by the shortest wet line. It does not stop to fight; it cuts in passing and is three reed-beds away when the wound starts to burn.

slough_scaleshield.name: Scaleshield
slough_scaleshield.description: A heavy-bodied krait behind a shield cut from one scale of a stranded leviathan, wider than a door. It lies across the causeways into the Brinks and nothing gets past that it has not let past.

slough_skin_reader.name: Skin-Reader
slough_skin_reader.description: A scholar of the hanging library who reads the old skins by touch, the scars and the patterns, and can tell a snake how it was healed last time. Mostly that is enough to heal it again.

slough_gourdslinger.name: Gourdslinger
slough_gourdslinger.description: A krait with a rack of sealed marsh-gourds slung across its back and a sling in each hand, one for stones and one for gourds. The gourds are filled at the milking-posts, and the Slough are not careful about which.

slough_hookfang_wrangler.name: Hookfang Wrangler
slough_hookfang_wrangler.description: A krait who hunts eels in the brine-channels with a barbed trident and a line, and has found the same tools bring a soldier off a causeway just as well. It holds what it hooks until the hooked thing stops arguing.

slough_siltcoil.name: Siltcoil Ambusher
slough_siltcoil.description: A mud-coloured krait who lies in the silt of a channel with only its hood and glaive-tip showing and waits, sometimes for days. Brink children are taught to step over still water, never into it.

slough_glaive_sister.name: Glaive-Sister
slough_glaive_sister.description: One of an order of duellists who settle the Slough's disputes in front of the hanging skins, so the old ones can watch. They open a vein first and let the other one decide how much longer it wants to move.

slough_yellowbelly_matriarch.name: Yellowbelly Matriarch
slough_yellowbelly_matriarch.description: A brood-mother of the yellowbelly line, gold underneath and black above, wearing a girdle of her children's first skins. Her venom is the strongest in the Brinks, and she is the only one who decides who gets milked for the gourds.

slough_skinbanner_elder.name: Skinbanner Elder
slough_skinbanner_elder.description: An elder who carries a pole hung with the skins of every Slough who died on this march, so that they can still see it. Where the banner goes the young fight harder, because they are being watched by the dead.

slough_ringwall.name: Ringwall
slough_ringwall.description: A four-armed krait as long as a barge, two hands on leviathan-scale shields and two on hooked tridents, whose body is the wall of whatever camp it lies around. The Slough do not build palisades. They ask a Ringwall.

slough_silt_slider.name: Silt-Slider
slough_silt_slider.description: A long glossy krait that rides the wet silt like a sled, tail paddling, a hooked sabre in each hand. Sliders run the Brinks' borders and are the reason the Compact's bone-sleds no longer take the trench road.

slough_hundredcoat.name: Hundredcoat
slough_hundredcoat.description: A four-armed krait three wagons long that has kept every skin it ever shed and wears them all, lacquered, layer over layer, so that it rattles like a reed-bed when it moves. Strip a coat off it and there is always another underneath.

slough_eldest_skin.name: The Eldest Skin
slough_eldest_skin.title: Who Has Shed Ninety Times
slough_eldest_skin.description: The ruler of the Slough, because she has shed more times than anyone alive: ninety skins, every one hung in order in the great library at the trench edge. She remembers the night the water left as the night the world was handed to her people, and nobody has been able to tell her otherwise.

slough_kesh.name: Kesh
slough_kesh.title: the Four-Handed
slough_kesh.description: The Eldest Skin's champion, a four-armed krait the length of a street who has never lost a duel in front of the library. Kesh is not cruel. Kesh simply holds on, with four hands and the whole of that body, until the argument is over.

slough_mother_ashgourd.name: Mother Ashgourd
slough_mother_ashgourd.title: Keeper of the Bitter Gourds
slough_mother_ashgourd.description: The keeper of the milking-posts, grey around the hood, who has filled every gourd the Slough have thrown for sixty years and brewed the antivenom for the ones that broke at home. She sells neither, and she has been asked.

slough_teshk.name: Teshk
slough_teshk.title: Who Bites Last
slough_teshk.description: A lean grey-banded duellist who fought his first Glaive-Sister at nine sheddings and has never been bitten since. He believes, sincerely, that the Ebb was done for the Slough, and that every army marching through the Brinks is a guest that has stayed too long.

slough_husk.name: Shed Husk
slough_husk.description: An empty skin, still standing in the shape of the snake that left it, hood up. It blocks the way until the wind takes it.

slough_great_husk.name: Great Husk
slough_great_husk.description: The lacquered outer coat of a giant, four empty sleeves and a hood as big as a tent, left upright on the field like a cast-off suit of armour.

slough_tail_segment.name: Coil
slough_tail_segment.description: A length of banded krait body. Strike it and the head feels it.
